company_analyst.what_they_do: Alaska Bush air carrier, HQ 6400 Carl Brady Drive, Anchorage. Their own about page: 'Air cargo shipping is our primary business.' and 'In Bush Alaska, where air service is the only way to receive and send furniture, clothing, food, medical supplies and more, the runway is a community's lifeline.' Lines of business: scheduled freight on a published Mon-Sat timetable out of seven bush hubs; bypass and USPS mail; charter (passenger and freight) quoted by phone or web form; scheduled passenger service; a UPS rural delivery contract ('Ryan Air has a contract with UPS only to deliver UPS parcels at our seven stations and to the villages served out of each hub'); ground handling for other carriers (Partners page lists Northern Air Cargo, Everts Air Cargo, Lynden Air Cargo, Alaska Airlines Air Cargo, Aleutian Airways); Priority Letter and Priority Freight; intervillage and backhaul tiers; maintenance bases in Anchorage and Unalakleet. No published cold-chain product. Tariff says 'Ryan Air does not offer insurance.'
company_analyst.size_note: The company publishes numbers that disagree with each other, which is itself a finding. Homepage: '24 aircraft out of eight hubs, proudly serving 80 villages'. About page: '24 aircraft out of eight hubs. We serve over 70 villages and employ over 180 people.' Destinations page: '25 aircraft out of eight hubs, serving 80 villages'. Parent Saltchuk Aviation: '20 aircraft from seven strategic hubs', 'over 70 villages', 'over 150 dedicated professionals'. So headcount 150-180+, fleet 20-25, villages 70-80, hubs 7-8.

'The Fuel Surcharge has been discontinued.' 'Flat rates have been discontinued.' Liability capped at '$.50 per pound, but not less than $50.00 per shipment, unless a higher value is declared', valuation charge $.50 per $100.00 declared. people_finder.ownership: MATERIAL CORRECTION. Ryan Air is NOT independently family owned. It joined the Saltchuk Family of Companies in December 2022 (saltchukaviation.com, corroborated by ch-aviation and Cargo Facts). It is still operated and managed by the Ryan family, third generation. The company's own about page says 'Ryan Air remains a family and native company managed by the third generation of Ryan family', which is true of MANAGEMENT and does not mention Saltchuk ownership. Founded 1953 in Unalakleet by Wilfred Ryan Sr. and Eva Ryan; Wilfred P. Ryan Jr. took over 1977; Lee Ryan named President 2019. Deal terms never disclosed. NO artifact may describe them as Alaska Native owned or family owned.

where_behind: SELF-SERVE RATE QUOTING. Ryan Air publishes a static tariff table and PDF. NAC lets a shipper price a real load with dimensions across 15 cargo types on five of Ryan Air's hubs. Lynden and Everts both offer quote or estimate requests. Ryan Air's shipper does the arithmetic or calls.

AUTOMATED STATUS NOTIFICATION. Lynden pushes email at five shipment milestones over five of Ryan Air's seven hubs. No notification of any kind was found on Ryan Air's site. Their model is pull-only, the customer goes and looks or dials 907-562-2227.

CUSTOMER ACCOUNT SELF-SERVICE. Everts has Customer Login, Lynden has EZ Commerce, Alaska Air Cargo has iCargo, even Bering Air has a My Points portal. Ryan Air's account onboarding is a Credit Application downloaded, printed and returned by mail or fax.

BYPASS MAIL VISIBILITY SPECIFICALLY. Everts' tracker names the Bypass Mail Order number as a searchable key with a worked example, 'B20ANC-1234'. Ryan Air's tracker, on the SAME Takeflite platform, prompts for 'your Booking, Air Waybill, Consolidation or Tracking Numbers' and does not name a bypass mail order number. For a carrier whose Western Alaska volume runs heavily on bypass mail, that is the sharpest single feature gap found, and it sits on a platform they already pay for.

ONLINE SHIPMENT CREATION. Everts has Create a Shipment, Alaska Air Cargo has Book a Shipment, Lynden books from templates, NAC lets you complete an AWB online. Ryan Air's tendering is through the mainline carrier or a phone call to one of seven stations.
competitor_analyst.not_behind_on: Ryan Air does have a working self-serve Takeflite freight tracker accepting multiple comma-separated numbers, which is more than Bering Air or Yute could be verified to offer.
competitor_analyst.where_could_lead: THE FIELD HAS ZERO AI. Across all seven carriers, on every page fetched, there is not one chatbot, virtual agent, AI assistant or AI-branded feature on the freight side. Nobody serving these villages has moved. No live chat verified on any freight site in the set. No published API or EDI verified for any of the seven. No proactive village-side arrival notification anywhere except Lynden's email milestones, and Lynden does not serve Aniak or Unalakleet on its scheduled list. No carrier in the set offers freight tracking on a mobile app.
competitor_analyst.jobs_to_be_done: THE REAL INCUMBENT IS A PHONE AND A COUNTER. For the job 'where is my freight and when does it land in the village', the alternative in use today is almost never software, it is a person, and every carrier in the set routes that job to a human in writing on its own site. Ryan Air says call the station of booking. Bering Air routes cargo to three station numbers. Yute says 'Talk to your station manager about what you're sending'. NAC's instruction is to fill out an AWB and email it. So the contested surface in Western Alaska freight is the phone line and the village counter, not a feature comparison between two websites, and every one of those calls is a cost every carrier is already paying.
competitor_analyst.confidence_limits: aceaircargo.com (403), flygrant.com (403) and beringair.com's homepage (bot-check) blocked the fetcher. Alaska Central Express was investigated and deliberately EXCLUDED because only a 2005 Wikipedia snapshot was fetchable. Every 'none found' means not present on pages that could be read, not proof of absence, and features behind customer logins are invisible by definition, so the true digital gap could be wider, never narrower.

in_production.who: C.H. Robinson, global 3PL ~15,000 employees, included as the reference case not a template
in_production.what: Generative-AI agents classifying inbound customer email, deciding whether it is a quote request, generating the quote and replying. Built on Azure AI.
in_production.outcome: Trade press reported: roughly 11,000 emails a day from shippers and carriers requesting pricing, and the AI answers about 2,000 customer quotes a day in just over 2 minutes, serving more than 2,000 truckload customers. Company self-reported figures (unaudited): over 3 million AI-performed shipping tasks, over 1 million AI quotes, 30 percent productivity increase 2023-2024, accompanied by headcount reduction.
in_production.reliability: authoritative for the deployment, vendor_claim for the company's own totals

in_production.who: Alaska Airlines dispatch, ~67 full-time dispatchers, with Air Space Intelligence 'Flyways'
in_production.what: ML route optimisation ingesting weather, winds, turbulence, airspace constraints and traffic, recommending routes to human dispatchers eight-plus hours ahead. NOT autonomous, the dispatcher decides on every recommendation.
in_production.outcome: Airline-reported: a six-month pilot cut fuel use by 480,000 gallons and avoided nearly 4,600 tons of CO2. All 67 dispatchers trained, partnership renewed. No acceptance-rate or minutes-saved figures published, which is a real gap in the public record. Airline-reported, not independently audited.

in_production.who: FAA Weather Camera Program with MIT Lincoln Laboratory (VEIA), across Alaska
in_production.what: Computer vision on existing FAA weather-camera feeds. Builds a reference clear image from 10 days of past imagery, uses an edge filter to find persistent landmarks, converts the ratio of visible edges to estimated visibility in miles. No new sensors.
in_production.outcome: Validated against Automated Surface Observing Stations at more than 90 percent accuracy detecting low-visibility conditions. The FAA's Safety Risk Management panel MANDATED that the raw camera image is always displayed alongside the estimate so a pilot can sanity-check the algorithm. The clearest example in this operating environment of AI deployed as an advisory layer on data that already existed, with a human cross-check designed in.

industry_analyst.ladder_reading: RULES AND DETERMINISTIC SOFTWARE still own most of this industry's real problems and almost nobody says so. Manifest arithmetic, weight and balance, tariff and rate tables, bypass mail eligibility, appointment slotting, compliance date tracking, dispatch legality. Exhaustively testable, same input must give same output, and an auditor or FAA inspector will ask you to show the rule. RETRIEVAL AND LOOKUP is where the quiet wins are and where the industry is genuinely behind. A SINGLE MODEL CALL on a messy input is the most proven AI rung in freight right now, classify an inbound email, read a scanned airbill, extract fields. A FIXED WORKFLOW with a human gate at the costly action is where the credible mid-size deployments sit, and both Flyways and VEIA are exactly this shape, surviving because the human stayed on the decision. A DYNAMIC AGENT with real autonomy is mostly a promise in this industry.

failures.what: Moffatt v. Air Canada, 2024 BCCRT 149, February 2024. The airline's website chatbot gave a passenger wrong bereavement-fare guidance. The tribunal found negligent misrepresentation, held the airline owed a duty of care, and flatly rejected the argument that the chatbot was a separate legal entity responsible for its own actions: 'It should be obvious to Air Canada that it is responsible for all the information on its website.' Damages C$812.02. A carrier owns what its bot tells a customer.

DPD, January 2024. A parcel carrier's customer-service chatbot was talked into ignoring its rules, swore at a customer and wrote a poem calling DPD 'a customer's worst nightmare'. DPD said 'an error occurred after a system update' and disabled the AI element immediately. The company had run AI in that chat successfully for years before one deploy broke it. The lesson is regression testing and adversarial input handling.

Convoy, October 19 2023. A $3.8bn-valued digital freight network built on ML load matching ceased operations. Stated precisely: Convoy did not fail because its ML was bad, it failed because software alone did not create defensible economics in a freight recession.

The everyday failure mode, described by a visibility vendor against its own interest: 'AI does not create accuracy, it amplifies whatever you feed it. If the underlying container data is incomplete, delayed, or conflicting, the AI does not just fail quietly. It confidently makes the wrong call.' The failures are not crashes, they are 'death by a thousand small errors that erode trust in the technology until the team stops using it and goes back to manual'.

industry_analyst.hype_flags: Agentic logistics and autonomous supply chain. Gartner names cross-enterprise negotiation, dynamic cost trade-offs and ethical judgment as poor agentic candidates before 2027 and warns that most current agentic capability improves the interface rather than the decision. Set-and-forget voice agents, where every freight number in the public record is vendor-supplied with no named customer and no third-party audit. Percentage-of-calls-deflected claims come almost entirely from vendor blogs. Predictive maintenance sold to small fleets, where the published research problem is too few failure samples to train on. Any AI ROI pitched without fixing record quality first.
industry_analyst.the_gap: There is essentially no published, independently verified AI deployment at the scale of a few-hundred-employee regional carrier. The documented cases split into Fortune-500 3PLs and mainline airlines with dedicated data teams on one side, and government safety programs that were free to the operator on the other. Neither is a template. Searching mid-tier carriers directly turns up broad talk of AI adoption and no specific published outcomes at all. That absence is itself the finding. The practical opening is UPSTREAM of AI: in this segment the data is on paper, on the phone, on a scale readout and in a station agent's head, and until it is captured it can't be modelled, forecast, tracked or deflected.

grounding_facts.fact: The USPS Office of Inspector General's audit of Alaska mail services (report 22-090-R22, site visits week of May 23 2022, issued September 28 2022) identified $346,649 in overpayments to air carriers attributable to inadequate payment review processes and missing claim documentation, no systematic tracking of mail movement across the remote network, shippers able to tender bypass mail without scheduled appointments or postage verification, and no standard weight threshold among air carriers for verifying shipments.

MIT Lincoln Laboratory's VEIA visibility algorithm tested more than 90 percent accurate at detecting low-visibility conditions when validated against Automated Surface Observing Stations, using only existing FAA web camera feeds and no specialized sensors. The FAA's Safety Risk Management panel required that the raw camera image always be displayed alongside the estimate so users can sanity-check the algorithm.

Gartner identifies cross-enterprise negotiation, dynamic cost trade-offs and ethical judgment as poor candidates for agentic AI before 2027, and warns that agent washing (relabelling conventional automation as agentic) raises the risk of misaligned investment and long-term lock-in.

C.H. Robinson receives roughly 11,000 emails a day from shippers and carriers requesting pricing, and its generative-AI agent answers about 2,000 customer quotes a day in just over two minutes, serving more than 2,000 truckload customers.

industry_analyst.confidence: Medium-high on state of play and the failure record. Medium-low on comparable-size deployments specifically: no independently verified AI deployment with published outcomes at a few-hundred-employee regional or rural carrier could be found, and that was searched for directly across LTL, regional air cargo and Part 135. That absence is reported as a finding rather than papered over.
